phases.title: Motor de deploy — runtime
phases.goal: Through the API a person creates project → environment → service (Git, Dockerfile or image, public or private) on a connected server and deploys it in the worker with live build logs, real container state, cancellation that kills the remote process, cleanup on every exit and honest reconciliation; 20 deploys and 20 create/delete cycles leave nothing orphaned.

tasks.title: Domain: project, environment and service inputs

acceptance.text: Project name and slug derivation (unique-safe, lowercase, collision suffix is the caller's job) and optional description validated into branded types
Environment name validator accepts any valid name; production/staging/development exported as suggestions only, kind stays free text (D23)

Service create/edit input validators for git (url, branch, context, Dockerfile, optional target), image (tag or digest, never implicit :latest), internal port and optional published port; no build-arg or env fields exist (D13)
classifyServiceEdit() pure: says whether an edit changes the source (requires redeploy) or only metadata
>=95% statement and branch coverage on the new validators; domain purity test still green

Git URL validator accepts only https:// and ssh (scp-style or ssh://) after parsing; rejects file:, ext::, git://, http://, javascript:/data:, embedded userinfo credentials, and values starting with '-' or containing whitespace/control chars

Branch, context path and Dockerfile path validators reject '..' segments, absolute paths, leading '-', NUL/newline and over-long values; image ref validator rejects whitespace, leading '-' and malformed digests

Slug derivation handles empty result (all non-ASCII/symbols), Unicode normalization, max length and reserved words with a deterministic fallback; ports validated as integers in 1-65535 and published port not equal to internal-only reserved ports

tasks.title: Domain: runtime policies (resource ledger, port preflight, reconcile diff, post-start polls)

acceptance.text: Resource ledger records workspace, per-attempt image, network, container and secrets file, and returns the cleanup set for each exit (SUCCESS, FAILED, CANCELLED, timeout, WORKER_CRASHED); the per-service running container is never in a failed attempt's cleanup set
Port preflight rejects collisions with other services on the server, the panel ports and ports in the parsed docker ps snapshot, returning PORT_IN_USE with the conflicting owner
Reconcile diff maps one docker ps snapshot to per-service container states, reports only changed services, and flags containers stopped or removed outside Noodara as discrepancies
Post-start poll schedule is 5 polls with 1 s to 8 s backoff, parameterised, and decides SUCCESS / START_FAILED / keep polling from inspect results
>=95% statement and branch coverage on the four modules
Resource ledger cleanup set is idempotent: computing and executing it twice yields the same set and a second run on already-removed resources is not an error

tasks.title: Domain: build-log chunker and runtime-log sanitizer

acceptance.text: Chunker flushes on time or size (defaults 250 ms / 16 KB, injected clock), assigns a monotonic seq per deployment and phase
Per-line cap (16 KB) truncates UTF-8-safely with a visible marker; per-phase cap (10 MiB) stops accepting and emits one truncation notice
Sanitizer strips ANSI escapes and replaces binary / invalid UTF-8 with a placeholder; never throws on arbitrary bytes (property test)
No I/O, no timers owned by the module; >=95% coverage

tasks.title: Deploy env knobs and deploy job budget

acceptance.text: Knobs NOODARA_DEPLOY_MAX_MS, NOODARA_DEPLOY_IDLE_MS, NOODARA_DEPLOY_CONCURRENCY, NOODARA_DEPLOY_LOG_MAX_BYTES, NOODARA_DEPLOY_LOG_FLUSH_MS/BYTES, NOODARA_DEPLOY_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS, NOODARA_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS, NOODARA_RUNTIME_LOG_TAIL, NOODARA_RUNTIME_LOG_FOLLOW_MAX_MS with research defaults and range validation
Every knob listed in turbo.json passThroughEnv and documented in .env.example (ADR 0003)
Deploy lock duration and Redis cancel-key TTL derived from NOODARA_DEPLOY_MAX_MS so BullMQ never reaps a live build (unit-tested at min and max)
Cross-knob validation: IDLE_MS <= MAX_MS, FLUSH_BYTES <= per-line cap, LOG_MAX_BYTES >= phase cap; invalid combinations fail boot with a named error without echoing unrelated env values

tasks.title: Activity actions and SSE event surface for projects, services and deployments

acceptance.text: Activity actions for project, environment, service and deployment lifecycle (incl. out-of-band container change) with metadata allowlists that cannot carry secrets
SSE surface is exactly service.updated, service.deleted, deployment.updated, deployment.log_chunk added to the server events (D22); no project.* or environment.* events
deployment.log_chunk payload is bounded and carries deploymentId, phase, seq; backpressure eviction behaviour of sse-broadcaster unchanged (existing tests green)

tasks.title: HTTPS-token clone contract test and askpass secret slot

acceptance.text: Askpass helper gets its own secret file name under <ws>/secrets (no longer the known_hosts slot), mode 600, removed with the workspace
Fixture serves an HTTPS (or HTTP basic-auth) git remote; clone with a token via askpass succeeds on 22.04 and 24.04, wrong token gives REPOSITORY_AUTH_FAILED
Token absent from ps, .git/config, remote URL and every captured stream
ADR 0008 open item 4 updated with the measured result

Deploy keys, HTTPS tokens and registry passwords never reach argv, URLs, env-over-SSH, logs, API responses, activity metadata or error messages; every streamed chunk goes through the Redactor; a per-run canary asserts it

tasks.title: Projects and environments API

acceptance.text: Create, edit, list and read projects (unique name case-insensitive, slug derived) and environments (unique per project); duplicates give a named 409

Archive and unarchive; delete only an archived project by typing its exact name (422 otherwise); the DB cascade covers environments, services, deployments, log chunks and service credentials (remote cleanup arrives in 12-14)
Environment routes reject an environment id from another project (404, no existence leak)
Every mutation writes an activity event; routes behind requireSession and origin guard like servers.ts

Malformed JSON, wrong content-type, unknown fields and oversized bodies on project/environment routes return 400/413/422 and the API keeps serving; name uniqueness race (two parallel creates differing only in case) yields one 201 and one named 409, never a 500
Project and environment endpoints return 401 without session and 403 on cross-origin mutation; unauthenticated requests never reveal whether an id exists

tasks.title: Services API: create, edit, read with derived status and guards

acceptance.text: Create git and image services only on a CONNECTED server with Docker; Dockerfile (git) services rejected when docker_buildkit_available is false (ADR 0008 G3)
Published port optional and off by default; collisions with other services on the server and the panel ports give PORT_IN_USE at create/edit time
Read returns every SVC-05 field with status from deriveServiceStatus (never a hand-written value); edit flags requiresRedeploy when the source changes
No route accepts a service, environment or server id outside the path's project; covered by a cross-project ownership test
Create and edit write activity events and publish service.updated

Service create/edit routes enforce body cap and reject malformed JSON with explicit 4xx; git URL scheme allowlist and path validators from 12-01 are applied server-side (not only in UI) and violations return a named 422

Port collision check at create/edit is race-safe: two concurrent creates claiming the same published port on one server result in exactly one success (DB-level constraint or lock), the other PORT_IN_USE

tasks.title: Private source credentials and delete-server guard

acceptance.text: Noodara generates an ed25519 deploy key per service, stores the private half encrypted at rest, returns only the public key
HTTPS token and registry password accepted write-only, encrypted at rest, never returned (responses expose only presence and type)
Credentials are rotated or removed when the source changes and deleted with the service (no orphan credentials rows)
Deleting a server with services returns 409 naming the blocking services (PROJ-05)

Deploy keys, HTTPS tokens and registry passwords never reach argv, URLs, env-over-SSH, logs, API responses, activity metadata or error messages; every streamed chunk goes through the Redactor; a per-run canary asserts it

Credential encryption uses authenticated encryption with a fresh random nonce per write; ciphertext tamper is detected on decrypt; deploy keys are generated with node:crypto (no Math.random) and each service gets a distinct key
Credential store never exposes plaintext through toJSON/inspect/error serialization; decrypt failures surface a closed-vocabulary code without ciphertext or key material

Credential inputs are validated server-side: token and registry password length capped, registry host and username validated, request body capped (413) and malformed JSON rejected (400) without echoing the submitted secret

tasks.title: Deploy queue and enqueue / read API

acceptance.text: POST /api/services/:id/deploy inserts a QUEUED deployment (source snapshot) and enqueues jobId deploy-<deploymentId>, answering immediately
A second deploy while one is active returns 409 DEPLOYMENT_IN_PROGRESS via the partial unique index, also under a concurrent race (two parallel POSTs, exactly one 201)
Archived project blocks deploys with a named error
GET deployment list per service (paginated, newest first) and detail; payload contains ids only, never secrets

If enqueue fails after the QUEUED insert (Redis down), the deployment is moved to FAILED with a named code or the insert is rolled back; no deployment stays QUEUED without a job; API answers a named 503, not a crash
Deployment list pagination caps page size (upper bound validated) and rejects malformed cursors/limits with 4xx; reading a deployment of another service/project returns 404
Deploy, cancel and other POST routes enforce the Fastify body cap (413) and reject unknown fields (422)

tasks.title: Deploy job core: run-deployment pipeline, deployment store and job handler (unit, fake ports)

acceptance.text: run-deployment sequences clone→build (or pull)→port preflight→replace container→post-start polls against fake ports, moving status only through the domain state machine; unit-tested per source type

Ledger cleanup runs in finally on SUCCESS, FAILED, timeout (BUILD_TIMEOUT vs BUILD_STALLED) and thrown errors; a failed build never touches the running container; superseded image removed only after the new container runs
Deployment store claims QUEUED→PREPARING atomically under a row lock, records commit SHA, and finishes with service status cache, activity event and service.updated / deployment.updated
Log output goes through an injected sink interface (real sink in 12-12)
SSH, Docker or Git failures surface as a closed-vocabulary code with an actionable message; raw remote stderr never reaches an API response and no remote failure crashes the API or the worker

Deploy keys, HTTPS tokens and registry passwords never reach argv, URLs, env-over-SSH, logs, API responses, activity metadata or error messages; every streamed chunk goes through the Redactor; a per-run canary asserts it
Worker job is idempotent against BullMQ stall/retry: a re-delivered job for a deployment already past QUEUED does not re-run remote commands (attempts 1 or state guard), proven by a stalled-job test

Per-deployment workspace path, image tag and container/network names are built only from validated ids; repo-controlled values (branch, Dockerfile path, git output) are never interpolated into shell strings, proven with hostile names ($(), backticks, ';', leading '-') in a fixture repo

tasks.title: Wire deploy worker and prove the pipeline on the real fixture

acceptance.text: Worker clones --depth 1 into /opt/noodara-deploy/<deploymentId> (SHA captured), builds noodara/<serviceId>:<deploymentId> with optional target, or pulls the image (registry login via --password-stdin into the per-deployment --config)
Port preflight against real docker ps; then old container replaced by noodara-<serviceId> on noodara-net-<serviceId> with --log-opt max-size/max-file; post-start polls decide SUCCESS or START_FAILED
Statuses move only through the domain state machine (QUEUED→PREPARING→BUILDING→DEPLOYING→SUCCESS/FAILED); service status cache recomputed and service.updated / deployment.updated published
failing-build ends FAILED/BUILD_FAILED with the previous container still running; max vs idle timeout give BUILD_TIMEOUT vs BUILD_STALLED

Ledger cleanup on every exit removes workspace, secrets, partial image and half-created container/network; superseded image removed after the new container runs; images compared by digest or RootFS.Layers, never .Id (ADR 0008)
src/worker.ts starts the deploy BullMQ worker (concurrency NOODARA_DEPLOY_CONCURRENCY, lock from deploy-job-budget, maxStalledCount 0) and closes it in the shutdown sequence

tasks.title: Build log pipeline: redact, persist, publish, resync, retention

acceptance.text: Every chunk passes the Redactor before persistence, Redis or SSE; a secret split across chunks never leaks
Chunks persisted append-only in deployment_log_chunks with seq, flushed on the 12-03 cadence, capped per line and per phase
deployment.log_chunk reaches an SSE client live during a node-api build; GET /api/deployments/:id/logs?since=<seq> returns only later chunks (no replay)
Retention job deletes chunks older than NOODARA_DEPLOY_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS without touching the deployment rows
A fixture that logs continuously for minutes keeps API RSS and SSE buffers bounded (no eviction of a healthy client); numbers recorded

Deploy keys, HTTPS tokens and registry passwords never reach argv, URLs, env-over-SSH, logs, API responses, activity metadata or error messages; every streamed chunk goes through the Redactor; a per-run canary asserts it

Log persistence failure (DB error) or Redis publish failure is logged without chunk content and does not fail or stall the deployment; seq has a unique constraint per deployment and phase and duplicate inserts are rejected
GET /api/deployments/:id/logs validates since as a non-negative integer, caps page size, requires session and returns 404 for deployments outside the caller's scope

tasks.title: Cancellation and worker-crash sweep

acceptance.text: Cancelling a QUEUED deployment removes the job and ends CANCELLED; it never executes any remote command

Cancelling a running build: Redis flag (TTL from 12-04) → killSupervisedOperation (kill -s TERM -- "-$pgid" under setsid -w, ADR 0008) → confirmed absence in ps → channel destroyed → cleanup → CANCELLED; only the worker transitions

After cancel no container, partial image, network, volume, workspace or secrets file remains, and docker system df Images/Containers/Local Volumes are unchanged; BuildKit build-cache records are excluded from the comparison (bounded growth only, retention is Phase 14 per ADR 0008)
Worker killed mid-build: startup sweep marks FAILED/WORKER_CRASHED, cleans per-deployment resources, never the per-service container
SSH, Docker or Git failures surface as a closed-vocabulary code with an actionable message; raw remote stderr never reaches an API response and no remote failure crashes the API or the worker

Cancel is idempotent and race-safe: cancelling a terminal deployment returns a named 409, a second cancel during CANCELLING is a no-op, and cancel racing with SUCCESS leaves exactly one terminal state

If killSupervisedOperation cannot confirm absence, deployment still ends FAILED/CANCEL_UNCONFIRMED-style named code with cleanup attempted and a warning activity event; the worker does not hang past a bounded timeout

tasks.title: Service operations and deletion: jobs, routes and remote cleanup (unit, fake ports)

acceptance.text: Redeploy, stop, restart and remove run as timed jobs through the deploy queue, write activity events (via services helpers) and publish service.updated; unit-tested with fake ports

Service delete stops and removes container, network, own images and workspace, then credentials and rows, publishing service.deleted; archived-project delete runs the same cleanup per service before the DB cascade; unit-tested with fake ports
Operations and deletes on a service with an active deployment return 409 DEPLOYMENT_IN_PROGRESS
SSH, Docker or Git failures surface as a closed-vocabulary code with an actionable message; raw remote stderr never reaches an API response and no remote failure crashes the API or the worker

Service delete is resumable and idempotent: a failure midway (SSH drop) leaves the service row with a named error and re-running the delete completes cleanup without errors on already-removed resources
Delete confirmation compares the exact name server-side; wrong/missing confirmation returns 422 and performs no remote command
Service operation and delete routes enforce the body cap (413), validate the confirmation field length and reject unknown fields (422)

tasks.title: Prove service operations and deletion on the real fixture

acceptance.text: Redeploy, stop, restart and remove are timed jobs that write activity events and publish service.updated
Deleting a service (exact name) stops and removes its container, network, own images and workspace, then its credentials and rows; service.deleted published
Deleting an archived project runs the same remote cleanup for every service before the DB cascade; an unreachable server leaves a named error, not orphaned rows pointing nowhere
Operations on a service with an active deployment return 409 DEPLOYMENT_IN_PROGRESS

tasks.title: Reconciliation tick

acceptance.text: Repeatable job every NOODARA_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS runs one docker ps --size=false per CONNECTED server, never per service, with commandMs timeout
Changed container state updates the cached service status and emits service.updated; unchanged state emits nothing
A container stopped or removed outside Noodara shows in the next tick and writes one activity event (no repeat on later ticks)
An unreachable server marks its services UNKNOWN, never STOPPED, and does not crash the tick for other servers
Reconcile ticks never overlap (a slow tick delays the next rather than running concurrently) and skip services with an active deployment so they cannot overwrite in-flight status

tasks.title: Runtime logs on demand

acceptance.text: GET tail returns the last N lines (default NOODARA_RUNTIME_LOG_TAIL, upper bound validated) with timestamps
Follow is a dedicated bounded stream (not a new global SSE type) that ends at NOODARA_RUNTIME_LOG_FOLLOW_MAX_MS and when the client disconnects, killing the remote docker logs
Output is redacted and sanitized (ANSI, binary) and never persisted
SSH, Docker or Git failures surface as a closed-vocabulary code with an actionable message; raw remote stderr never reaches an API response and no remote failure crashes the API or the worker
Concurrent follow streams are capped per server and per user with a named 429/409; tail validates N as a positive integer within the upper bound and rejects other values with 4xx

tasks.title: Leak canaries for the deploy engine

acceptance.text: Canaries for git-URL token, deploy key, registry password and a fixture build that prints a canary
Absence asserted in build logs, deployment_log_chunks, SSE stream, activity_events.metadata, every API response, docker inspect, docker history and the remote .git/config
pnpm security:scan-leaks includes the new file

Deploy keys, HTTPS tokens and registry passwords never reach argv, URLs, env-over-SSH, logs, API responses, activity metadata or error messages; every streamed chunk goes through the Redactor; a per-run canary asserts it

tasks.title: QA-08 soak: 20 deploys and 20 create/delete cycles

acceptance.text: 20 consecutive node-api deployments complete SUCCESS
20 service create/delete cycles leave no container, network, image or workspace; docker system df equal before and after, twice in a row without manual prune
Nightly runs the soak on 22.04 and 24.04 (NOODARA_SOAK=1) and fails on any surviving noodara.test=true resource
Soak records per-iteration duration and docker system df before/after to an artifact so leak regressions are visible, and fails when any iteration exceeds the deploy max timeout

tasks.title: Measured defaults, docs and phase verification

acceptance.text: Measured numbers recorded for every knob (flush, line and phase caps, reconcile interval and cost, timeouts, post-start polls, log tail/follow) with fixture and Ubuntu version
docs/deploy-engine.md describes the API surface, statuses, error codes and knobs in under two pages
ADR 0008 open item 6 closed with a green amd64 CI run of tests/integration/deploy-engine
Phase 12 requirements ticked in REQUIREMENTS.md and ROADMAP.md

phases.title: UI de Projects & Services y E2E de deploy
phases.goal: From the UI a person creates project, environment and service, deploys it watching the build narrated step by step and live logs in the inspector, sees the real container state, recovers from a failure with an actionable hint, and the critical Playwright E2E proves it against real fixtures.

tasks.title: API: delete environment with exact-name confirmation

acceptance.text: DELETE /api/projects/:projectId/environments/:environmentId requires the exact environment name in the body; a mismatch is 422 like project delete, an unknown or foreign-project id is 404
Deleting an environment that still has services is rejected with 409 ENVIRONMENT_NOT_EMPTY and changes nothing; an empty environment is deleted and environment.deleted is written to the activity log
Integration test in tests/integration/projects covers success, name mismatch, non-empty, foreign project and unauthenticated cases
error-codes.mdx and docs/deploy-engine.md list the new route and ENVIRONMENT_NOT_EMPTY

Environment delete is race-safe: a service created concurrently with the delete never leaves an orphan service row; either the delete returns 409 ENVIRONMENT_NOT_EMPTY or the create returns 404, never a 500 or dangling environment_id (check and delete in one transaction or under a row lock).

Environment delete route rejects malformed JSON, missing name field, unknown fields and oversized bodies with 400/413/422 and the API keeps serving; it requires a session (401) and passes the origin guard (403 cross-origin), and the 404/422 responses do not reveal whether an id exists in another project.

tasks.title: Events: updatedAt on service.updated and deployment.updated

acceptance.text: ServiceEventView and DeploymentEventView carry updatedAt (ISO string) equal to the row updated_at written in the same transaction as the change they announce
Every publisher of service.updated / deployment.updated passes the post-write updatedAt; a unit test fails if an event is built without it
The SSE type set stays at the four deploy-engine types (D22); no new event type is added
runtime-reconcile integration test asserts updatedAt on a reconcile-driven service.updated is >= the snapshot GET value

updatedAt on events is monotonic per entity: two rapid writes to the same service or deployment never publish an older updatedAt after a newer one, and the event payload carries no fields beyond the existing allowlisted view (no secrets, no errorMessage raw text).

tasks.title: Deployment step timeline: clone, build, start, verify

acceptance.text: Pure domain function deriveDeploymentSteps() returns exactly four steps (clone|pull, build, start, verify) each with state pending|running|success|failed|cancelled|skipped and startedAt/completedAt; image sources show pull and skip build; >=95% statement and branch coverage

A versioned migration adds nullable step timestamps to deployments; the worker records each step boundary in the same write as the status transition, so a crash never leaves a step running without a status that explains it
GET deployment views expose steps[] derived by the domain function; a failed deploy marks the failing step failed and later steps pending, a cancel marks the running step cancelled
runtime-pipeline integration test asserts four ordered steps with non-null durations on a node-api success and failed build step on failing-build

Step timestamps are written only through the domain state machine transition and a single DB write: a concurrent cancel and success leave step timestamps consistent with the one terminal status (no step left running on a terminal deployment); the migration is additive with nullable columns, applies cleanly on a DB with existing deployments, and old rows derive steps without throwing.

deriveDeploymentSteps is total over every deployment status and error code combination (property test over all statuses x source types): never throws, always returns exactly four steps in fixed order, and durations are never negative when clocks are skewed or completedAt precedes startedAt.

The migration is additive and reversible-safe: existing deployments keep null step timestamps, deriveDeploymentSteps returns a valid timeline for them from status alone, and boot on a database migrated mid-deploy never fails

tasks.title: Web: build-log fold by (phase, seq) over snapshot

acceptance.text: Pure foldBuildLog(state, input) merges GET pages and SSE deployment.log_chunk events ordered by phase (prepare, build, deploy) then seq, dropping duplicates and never reordering already-shown text
A gap in seq marks the state as needing resync with the exact (phase, since) cursor for GET /logs; a chunk older than the cursor is ignored (no replay)
Truncated SSE chunks are replaced by the full GET chunk with the same (phase, seq)
Property-style tests shuffle arrival order of snapshot pages and events and always converge to the same text; >=95% branch coverage

foldBuildLog is bounded: total retained text is capped (matching the server per-phase cap) with a visible truncation marker, a pathological flood of chunks or a gap that never resolves does not grow memory unbounded or loop on resync, and malformed chunk input (negative seq, non-integer, unknown phase) is dropped without throwing.

Log text is treated as inert data: chunk content containing ANSI/escape sequences, HTML or script tags and secret-looking canary strings is preserved verbatim as text by the fold and never interpreted, and the fold never logs chunk content.

tasks.title: Web: typed API client for projects, environments, services, deployments, logs

acceptance.text: deploy-api.ts exposes typed calls for every route in docs/deploy-engine.md used by the UI, built on the existing api-client error model; response types come from the control-plane schemas, not re-declared by hand
Credential calls are write-only: no client function or type reads a secret value back; tests assert the PUT body is never logged or kept in state

runtime-log-stream.ts reads the NDJSON follow stream with an AbortController, stops on abort, server end or RUNTIME_LOG_FOLLOW_LIMIT_REACHED and surfaces RUNTIME_LOGS_* codes as typed errors; tested with MSW
Every call has an explicit timeout; a network failure resolves to a typed error, never an unhandled rejection

api-client never forwards or logs secrets: request bodies of credential calls are excluded from any error object, thrown message, console output and retry/telemetry payloads, and an error response echoing the submitted secret is not surfaced to callers (canary test).

Mutating calls send credentials: same-origin cookies and the origin-guard-compatible headers, and a 401 from any call resolves to the existing session-expired handling instead of being retried or swallowed; non-idempotent POSTs (deploy, cancel) are never auto-retried on timeout.

runtime-log-stream is bounded and safe: a partial NDJSON line split across reads is reassembled, a malformed line is skipped without ending the stream, a line over a client cap is truncated, total buffered lines are capped, and the reader is released (reader.cancel) on abort, server end and error with no leaked connection.

tasks.title: E2E stack: deploy host, git host and registry for Playwright

acceptance.text: The e2e stack can start the deploy-engine host (sshd + dockerd, git host with node-api and failing-build repos, pinned-digest registry mirror) by reusing tests/integration/helpers/deploy-engine.ts, never a second copy of its setup
Specs get a handle exposing the SSH connection data, repo URLs and an exec() into the deploy host to curl the published port and list containers, images, networks and workspaces
Teardown stops every container it started even when a spec fails; existing specs keep starting only what they used before (no deploy host unless requested)
A smoke spec starts the deploy host, runs docker info inside it and tears down cleanly

Deploy host teardown is leak-free and idempotent: running global-teardown twice, or after a crashed setup, removes every container, network and volume carrying the e2e label without erroring, only touches resources it created (run-scoped label, never a host-wide prune), and uses per-run randomly generated credentials for the registry and SSH keys that are not written to the repo or test logs.

The deploy host handle has a bounded startup timeout and a readiness check (sshd, dockerd, git host and registry all answering) before specs run; a failure to start fails the run with a named error instead of hanging, and exec() has a per-call timeout and returns exit code and redacted output.
Per-run SSH keys, registry htpasswd and git token come from crypto-grade generators in the shared helper, never fixed literals, and are written only to the run temp dir

tasks.title: CI debt: @rowmenu 440x956 and a11y-fallbacks reduced-motion flake

acceptance.text: Root cause of the @rowmenu 440x956 failure is reproduced by a failing test first and documented in the commit body; the fix is in product code unless the test assumption is proven wrong
servers-list.spec.ts and a11y-fallbacks.spec.ts pass 10 consecutive runs locally with a fresh stack
No retry, timeout bump or skip is added to hide the failure

The fix introduces no viewport-specific hack or layout change at other breakpoints: the RowMenu stays operable by keyboard and pointer at 440x956 and at 375, 900 and 1280 widths, the menu is not clipped by overflow containers, and the focus trap/return and Escape behavior from Phase 8 still pass.

tasks.title: Web: deploy-engine events and shared sequence reconciliation

acceptance.text: The frame parser accepts the four deploy-engine types and drops malformed frames like it does for server types

One generic pure reconcile function keyed by id + updatedAt is used by both the server store and the new service/deployment stores; reconcileSnapshot for servers keeps its tests green on top of it (REC-02: same function)

Reorder tests: for every permutation of (snapshot in flight, updated event, deleted event) the final state equals the newest write; an event never regresses a newer snapshot and a delete is never resurrected
The shell keeps exactly one EventSource; log chunks are routed to subscribers by deploymentId and never stored for deployments nobody is viewing

Event stream resilience: after an EventSource reconnect the shell refetches service and deployment snapshots and reconciles them with the same function, an event for an unknown id or with a missing/invalid updatedAt is ignored or triggers a refetch without crashing, and a deployment.log_chunk for an unsubscribed deployment is dropped without allocating per-deployment state.

Log subscriptions are cleaned up: unsubscribing (unmount, navigation, inspector close) removes the handler so no chunk is delivered or retained afterwards, and subscribe/unsubscribe over 1000 cycles leaves zero registered handlers (leak test).

tasks.title: Shell: Projects hierarchy in the sidebar and projects list

acceptance.text: Sidebar NavTree shows Projects -> Environment -> Service as a hierarchy with Servers, Activity and Settings as peers; active path is highlighted and keyboard navigation works as in Phase 8
Projects list with a create sheet (name, optional description; slug shown as derived); archived projects are visually separated and say they reject deploys
Empty state teaches the hierarchy in one sentence and offers one primary action; no coming-soon copy and no env vars mention beyond the stated v0.2 limit
The sidebar updates live from service.updated/service.deleted events without a reload

Project and service names rendered in the sidebar, list and sheet are escaped as text (a name like or a very long name with no spaces renders inert and truncated with the full name in a tooltip/accessible label), and the create sheet submit is disabled while pending so a double click sends one POST and a server 409 duplicate name shows in place.

Sidebar live updates are bounded and correct: a service.deleted for the currently active route navigates to the project view with a notice instead of a broken page, and a burst of 200 service.updated events renders without re-rendering unaffected tree branches beyond the changed node.
The Activity page passes project and service lookups to ActivityRow (13-15), so rows for existing projects and services link to them and rows for deleted ones stay plain text

tasks.title: Project and environment management with exact-name confirmation

acceptance.text: Project view lists environments and their services; create environment suggests production, staging, development and accepts any valid name, showing the server-side validation error in place
Edit project, archive, unarchive and delete (archived only) are available; delete and environment delete require typing the exact name using confirm-match from packages/ui
Deleting a non-empty environment shows the ENVIRONMENT_NOT_EMPTY recovery (remove its services first), never a raw error
ConfirmByNameDialog is generic and reused by service delete in 13-12

Destructive dialogs are safe: ConfirmByNameDialog keeps the confirm button disabled until the exact name matches (case and whitespace sensitive), submits once, is dismissed by Escape, returns focus to the trigger, and the typed value is never put in the URL; a 404 on delete (already deleted elsewhere) is treated as done and refreshes the list.
Environment and project form errors map server 409/422 codes to field-level messages in place, never raw server text, and the form state survives a failed submit so the user's input is not lost.

tasks.title: Service create and edit: source control, server picker, private credentials

acceptance.text: Segmented control Git / Dockerfile / Image switches the fields; validation reuses @noodara/domain validators client-side and shows the server error when they disagree
Server picker lists only CONNECTED servers with Docker available; other servers are absent, and an empty picker explains how to connect one

Repo token / SSH key / registry password are write-only inputs: after saving the UI shows only configured/not configured with replace and remove, the value is cleared from state and never rendered, logged or put in the URL
No env var or build arg fields exist; the sheet states the v0.2 limit once (variables arrive later) without coming-soon wording
Editing the source shows that a redeploy is needed before the change takes effect (classifyServiceEdit)

Credential fields: after save or on cancel/sheet close the secret is removed from React state, form defaults and any persisted draft (no localStorage/sessionStorage/URL), inputs use autocomplete=off and type=password, the field is not included in error reports, and a failed save does not echo the submitted value in the UI error.

Client-side validation mirrors the server allowlist for git URLs: https:// and ssh forms are accepted and file:, ext::, git://, http://, javascript:, embedded userinfo, leading '-' and path '..' are rejected inline before any request is sent, and the SSH deploy-key flow shows only the public key with a copy action.

Create/edit submit prevents duplicate submissions (disabled while pending, single POST on double click) and a server PORT_IN_USE or BUILDKIT_UNAVAILABLE-style error is mapped to the relevant field with an actionable hint.

tasks.title: Service view: derived status, Deploy, history and operations

acceptance.text: Status pill shows the derived status (running, stopped, deploying, failed, never_deployed) and UNKNOWN honestly with what it means; never a stored value
Exactly one primary action, Deploy; redeploy, stop, restart, remove container and delete service live in the overflow menu; delete requires the exact service name
An active deployment shows Cancel; DEPLOYMENT_IN_PROGRESS and DEPLOYMENT_NOT_CANCELLABLE show their recovery copy
Deployment history lists status, trigger, short commit SHA (mono), duration and relative time, paginated by cursor, and updates live from deployment.updated
Archived project: Deploy is disabled with the reason stated

Action safety: Deploy and overflow actions are disabled while a request is pending so a double click enqueues exactly one deployment, and a 409 DEPLOYMENT_IN_PROGRESS from a race refreshes state instead of showing an error toast loop; cancel is available only while the deployment is cancellable and a second click is a no-op.

Deployment history pagination handles an invalid or expired cursor by resetting to the first page, merges deployment.updated events by id without duplicating rows across pages, and the commit SHA and trigger values from the server are rendered as inert text.

ServiceSheet (13-11) is reachable: the project view has a New service action per environment that opens it in create mode, and the service view has Edit that opens it in edit mode; after save the lists update without reload

tasks.title: Deploy narration and classified errors

acceptance.text: Narration shows clone (or pull), build, start, verify with per-step state and duration, reusing the DiscoveryStep visual treatment (extracted, not copied)
Every DEPLOYMENT_ERROR_CODES value maps to a title and an actionable recovery; a test fails if a code is added without copy
errorMessage from the server is never rendered as raw text; only the classified copy and, when present, the sanitized last build log lines in the inspector
Reduced motion: the running-step indicator does not animate

Unknown or future error codes fall back to a generic classified copy with a safe recovery (never undefined, never the raw errorMessage), and sanitized last build log lines shown with an error are length-capped, rendered as text and pass through a client-side secret-pattern guard that masks canary secrets even if the server missed them.
The service view renders DeploymentSteps for the latest or selected deployment and updates it live from deployment.updated

tasks.title: Inspector: live build logs and on-demand runtime logs

acceptance.text: Build logs open in the @inspector parallel-route slot (not a modal) for the selected deployment: GET snapshot first, then SSE chunks folded with foldBuildLog; reload mid-build shows the same text without replay
Monospace, auto-scroll while at bottom, Jump to bottom appears when the user scrolls up; ANSI is already sanitized server-side and rendered as text only (no innerHTML)
Runtime logs load on demand with a tail selector and a Follow toggle using runtime-log-stream; follow stops on navigation, toggle off and server limit, and says why
Inspector closes with Escape and returns focus; at 375 px it becomes a full-height sheet; with no selection the slot stays zero width as in Phase 8

Log panels are bounded in the DOM: the build log keeps a capped number of rendered lines (virtualized or windowed) with a visible truncated notice, a flood of 100k lines keeps the main thread responsive (no per-chunk full re-render), and opening/closing the inspector 50 times leaves no live EventSource subscription, stream reader or timer.

Runtime follow lifecycle: leaving the page, toggling Follow off, changing tail, or unmount aborts the fetch and the server-side docker logs is terminated; a 429 or capacity error for concurrent follow streams shows its typed recovery copy and the Follow toggle returns to off; a server limit reached message states the reason once.

Inspector selection comes from the route (deployment id in the URL), a deployment id outside the caller's scope or that no longer exists renders a not-found state without a thrown error or infinite loading, and the panel does not leak the previous deployment's text when the selection changes.
Selecting a deployment in the history opens its build logs in the inspector, and the service toolbar has a Logs action that opens runtime logs

tasks.title: Activity copy for project, environment, service and deployment actions

acceptance.text: Every action in PROJECT_ACTIONS, ENVIRONMENT_ACTIONS, SERVICE_ACTIONS, DEPLOYMENT_ACTIONS and DEPLOY_ENGINE_ACTIONS has human copy; a test iterates the domain arrays and fails on any missing action
Rows link to the project or service when it still exists and render plain text when it was deleted

Activity copy renders names and metadata as text only and tolerates missing, null or unexpected metadata keys and unknown actions with a generic fallback row (never throws or shows raw JSON), and links to a project or service are built only from validated ids (never from metadata strings) with no open-redirect or javascript: hrefs.

tasks.title: E2E critical deploy path (QA-09)

acceptance.text: Playwright creates project -> environment -> service from node-api through the UI, deploys, sees live build logs in the inspector and the four steps succeed
The service answers on its published port (curl from inside the deploy host returns the node-api JSON)
A failing-build service ends FAILED with the BUILD_FAILED copy and recovery visible, and the previously running container of the first service is untouched
Cancelling an in-progress build ends CANCELLED and the deploy host has no leftover noodara containers, images, networks or workspaces for it
Ownership: a service id from project A requested under project B is not found in the UI and API
Runs in the CI main workflow and in nightly e2e-repeat; 20/20 locally with pnpm test:e2e:repeat before close

Test hygiene: E2E credentials, deploy keys and registry passwords are generated per run with crypto.randomBytes, never committed, and a canary secret entered in the service form and used in a clone/registry login is asserted absent from the page DOM, console logs, network responses, Playwright trace/HAR artifacts, and the uploaded CI artifacts.

The e2e deploy spec is deterministic: it waits on observable UI state (step statuses, SSE-driven updates) rather than fixed sleeps, uses a bounded per-test timeout below the CI job timeout, cleans up its created project/services in afterEach even on failure, and passes with Playwright retries disabled.

The cancel scenario also asserts the cancelled deployment's build process is gone from ps on the deploy host (not only that Docker resources are absent), and that reloading the page mid-build shows the same log text with no duplicated or lost lines.

tasks.title: UI fixes from the Phase 13 DoD review

acceptance.text: Light theme: the active NavTree item and every error/notice caption on the new screens meet WCAG AA 4.5:1; NavTree no longer emits both text-ink and text-ink-secondary on the active item; the runtime "no container yet" notice uses neutral, not error, color
Sheet returns focus to the element that opened it when closed by Escape, Cancel or overlay click, also when used controlled without a Trigger
Service names in the project page truncate with ellipsis and keep a readable minimum width when the repository URL is very long; the full name stays available (title or tooltip)
Service facts show "Last changed" as relative time only, never a raw ISO string; the deployment step timeline connector does not cross step icons
Fixes follow noodara-ux-apple tokens; no new colors, shadows or gradients

tasks.title: UI DoD for new screens and screenshot approval

acceptance.text: Measured contrast meets the design-system thresholds on every new screen in both themes
Projects, project, service, create sheets and inspector render without horizontal scroll or clipping at 375, 900, 1280 and 1920 px in light and dark
Reduced motion removes non-essential animation on the new screens
noodara-ux-review report for the new screens has no BLOCK; screenshots in both themes are saved under docs/ui-review/ and the user approved them

Every interactive element on the new screens is keyboard reachable in logical order with a visible focus ring, dialogs and sheets trap focus and restore it on close, status is conveyed by text or icon and not color alone, and an axe scan on each new screen in both themes reports zero serious or critical violations.

Long content stress: a project name of 200 characters, a service with a 300-character repo URL, and a 10,000-line build log render without horizontal page scroll or overlapping at 375 px, in both themes.
brand.spec.ts reflects the Projects nav entry from 13-09 (4 sidebar links) and the full pnpm test:e2e run is green

tasks.title: Docs: first deploy guide

acceptance.text: first-deploy.mdx walks project -> environment -> service -> deploy -> logs with the exact UI labels, states the v0.2 limits (no env vars or build args, stop-then-start downtime) without coming-soon wording
'deploy-services' is removed from the scope exclusions and the site builds

first-deploy.mdx is verified against reality: every UI label quoted in the guide exists in the web source (a test greps the labels), internal links resolve, code blocks contain no real-looking secrets or tokens (placeholders only), and the page appears in meta.json navigation order and in the site search index.

tasks.title: Navigate to the new project or service after create

acceptance.text: Creating a project closes the sheet and navigates to /projects/<newId>; creating a service navigates to /projects/<pid>/services/<newId>; editing keeps the user where they are
Navigation happens only after the create response succeeds; a failed create keeps the sheet open with the input intact
The sidebar shows the new project or service without reload, and focus lands on the new page heading
deploy.spec.ts follows the new flow (no clicking the new row after create) and passes

tasks.title: Deterministic @sheet-drag re-grab mid-close E2E

acceptance.text: Root cause of the e2e-repeat iteration 11 failure (server-sheet.spec.ts:587, re-grab offset 266 > 200) is identified and written in the commit body: test timing assumption or a real product bug in re-grab tracking
The spec drives the mid-close state deterministically (e.g. waits on the panel position or a frame count, not wall-clock); no threshold bump, retry, timeout increase or skip
If the product re-grab tracking is wrong, a unit test reproduces it first and the fix keeps 1:1 tracking from the on-screen position
server-sheet.spec.ts @sheet-drag passes 30 consecutive runs locally

tasks.title: Monotonic clock in ssh contracts elapsed measurement

acceptance.text: attemptConnect measures elapsedMs with performance.now() (monotonic) instead of Date.now(), so a wall-clock adjustment cannot report 4991 ms for a 5000 ms readyTimeout; assertions and thresholds unchanged

tasks.title: Phase 13 verification and requirement close-out

acceptance.text: pnpm test:integration and pnpm test:e2e are green with port 3000 free; LOG-04, REC-02, QA-09 and DOCS-01 are marked complete with evidence
OPEN_QUESTIONS 4-6 and the 13 assumptions are either confirmed by the user or still listed as open

Phase close-out leaves no skipped or quarantined tests: a grep of apps/, packages/ and tests/ for .skip, .only, test.fixme and retries added in phase 13 returns nothing without a linked justification, and pnpm security:scan-leaks passes including any new phase 13 spec.

A final pnpm test:e2e:repeat run (20/20) and pnpm lint, typecheck and boundaries are recorded with command output in the SUMMARY, and docs/deploy-engine.md route list matches the registered Fastify routes (a check fails if a route exists without documentation).

phases.title: Hardening y gate de release v0.2
phases.goal: v0.1 operators stop paying owed debt (unbounded logs, piling .env backups, a 1.2 GB image, POSIX scanner false positives), the Phase 12/13 security and UI debt is closed, and v0.2.0 ships after a READY gate against roadmap §7.8 on a real VPS.

tasks.title: Compose: log rotation on every production service

acceptance.text: All six services in docker-compose.yml (postgres, redis, migrate, api, worker, web) declare logging driver json-file with max-size and max-file, through one shared YAML anchor
A unit test parses docker-compose.yml and fails if any service lacks the logging block or the limits differ from the documented values
compose-stack.test.ts asserts via docker inspect that a running api container has the configured LogConfig
docs/install.md says where logs live and their size bounds

Log limits are bounded values (max-size and max-file are positive, max-size in the documented range) and the postgres and redis services keep their existing healthchecks and volumes unchanged by the logging block; the unit test fails on a missing or empty logging.options

tasks.title: Installer: prune .env.bak-* keeping the newest N

acceptance.text: After writing a backup, the installer deletes older .env.bak-* files next to .env and keeps the newest N (default 5, overridable by NOODARA_ENV_BACKUPS_KEEP, validated as a positive integer)
Pruning only matches <env path>.bak-<14 digits>; files with other names, symlinks and directories are never removed
idempotent-rerun.test.ts runs more than N upgrades and asserts exactly N backups remain, each mode 600, and the newest one matches the pre-upgrade .env
The code stays POSIX sh and pnpm check:posix-sh passes

The backup is written atomically with mode 600 from creation (umask set before write, or temp file then rename), and a failure of the prune step (unreadable dir, rm error) never aborts the upgrade nor deletes the freshly written backup or .env

NOODARA_ENV_BACKUPS_KEEP values of 0, negative, non-numeric, empty or with whitespace/shell metacharacters fall back to a clear error or the default 5 without running rm, and file names with spaces or leading '-' are handled safely (rm -- with quoted paths, no word splitting)
Pruning orders backups by the 14-digit timestamp in the name, not by mtime, so a touched or restored older backup is not kept over a newer one; same-second duplicates do not collide

tasks.title: check-posix-sh: remove false positives with regression tests

acceptance.text: $(( )) arithmetic expansion, the [[:space:]] POSIX character class, $' inside comments and (( inside heredoc bodies are not reported; each case has its own regression test
The real bashisms are still reported: [[ ]] tests, (( )) arithmetic commands, $'...' outside comments, arrays, local, $EUID; each has a test that keeps failing
The scanner's output format and exit codes do not change (ci.yml keeps using it unchanged)

The scanner never throws or hangs on empty files, files without trailing newline, unterminated heredocs, quoted heredoc delimiters (<<'EOF', <<-EOF) and CRLF input; unterminated heredocs are reported as a finding, not silently treated as comment text, and a bashism after the heredoc terminator is still reported

A real bashism on the same line as a suppressed pattern (for example $(( )) followed by [[ ]] or a trailing comment containing $') is still reported, so the false-positive fixes cannot mask real findings

tasks.title: install.sh: retire the check-posix-sh workarounds

acceptance.text: The workarounds documented in install.sh (awk division instead of $(( )), ((-substring avoidance in heredocs, [:space:] avoidance) are replaced with the direct POSIX form, and the comments that justify them are removed
pnpm check:posix-sh passes on the new install.sh and the full installer suite is green on 22.04 and 24.04

After removing the workarounds, install.sh arithmetic and character-class behavior is verified on dash (the 22.04/24.04 /bin/sh) with a unit test that executes the changed expressions, including empty/zero/non-numeric operands, rather than only passing the static scan

tasks.title: Control-plane image under 600 MB without breaking module resolution

acceptance.text: The runner stage ships only production dependencies plus compiled dist (pnpm deploy --prod or an equivalent), not the whole pruned workspace
control-plane-image.test.ts fails if the image is 600 MB or larger (docker image inspect Size) and records the measured size

The four entrypoints (api dist/server.js, worker dist/worker.js, migrate dist/db/migrate.js, CLI dist/cli/index.js) start from the new image and the argon2 native binding loads on the image's own architecture
ADR 0003 records the new runtime layout and the measured size before and after

The runner image runs as a non-root user, contains no devDependencies, build toolchain, pnpm store or source maps beyond dist, and the .dockerignore excludes .env*, .git and node_modules so no secret or local env file can be copied into any layer; a test inspects docker history/filesystem for these

The 600 MB threshold is a named constant checked against the actual built image in the same test run (not a hard-coded measured value), and the size check fails with the measured size in its message; the multi-arch (arm64) image is also under the limit or the arm64 size is recorded

tasks.title: Git host key pinning: bundled keys + TOFU (domain, ssh, git)

acceptance.text: packages/domain exports the published host keys for github.com, gitlab.com and bitbucket.org, plus a pure validator/parser for an OpenSSH host key line (host, type, base64 key) with ≥95% branch coverage
GIT_SSH_COMMAND uses StrictHostKeyChecking=yes with a known_hosts file written from a bundled or pinned key; accept-new no longer appears anywhere in packages/

For a host without a bundled key, an allowlisted ssh-keyscan template with an explicit timeout returns the key and the clone is pinned to it (persisting that key per service for later deploys is 14-07); the clone never starts with accept-new or an unpinned host, and existing deploy-engine integration tests keep passing by supplying their fixture host key
A host key mismatch is classified as GIT_HOST_KEY_MISMATCH from git/ssh output (ADR 0008 text classification), with a fixture per Ubuntu version

The bundled host keys have a recorded provenance (official publication URL and fetch date) and a test asserts each bundled line parses, has the expected type (ed25519/rsa/ecdsa) and fingerprint SHA256 matching the vendor-published fingerprint constant, so a typo or substituted key fails CI

The host key parser rejects lines with option prefixes, embedded newlines, wildcards or hashed hosts, leading '-', non-base64 key bodies, mismatched type/key blob, and over-long input; and the known_hosts file content is built only from validated parts (host validated, no interpolation of repo-controlled text into shell), proven with hostile hosts ($(), backticks, ';', spaces)

The ssh-keyscan template output is treated as untrusted: only the single requested host's key lines of an accepted type are returned, extra lines or hosts are dropped, a keyscan timeout or empty output fails closed with a named error, and the clone never proceeds without a pinned key even when keyscan fails

Non-default ports and ssh:// URLs with port (host key stored as [host]:port) pin and match correctly, and host comparison is case-insensitive and ignores trailing dots so a mismatch cannot be bypassed by alternate spellings

tasks.title: Git host key pinning: persistence, runtime wiring, reset

acceptance.text: A versioned migration adds a nullable git host key (host + key line) to services; the first SSH clone of a non-bundled host stores it and later clones pin it

The integration test against the real sshd+dockerd fixture covers: first clone stores the key, second clone pins it, a rotated host key fails the deployment FAILED/GIT_HOST_KEY_MISMATCH with an actionable message and no workspace left behind
The operator CLI can forget a service's pinned key (noodara services reset-host-key <serviceId>) and writes an activity event without the key material
HTTPS clones are unaffected (contracts-https-token stays green); error-codes.mdx and docs/deploy-engine.md document the new code and the reset

The TOFU store is race-safe: two concurrent first clones of the same non-bundled host for one service result in exactly one stored key (conditional update where git_host_key is null) and the loser verifies against the winner's key instead of overwriting it; a rotated key is never auto-replaced

The migration is additive with nullable columns, applies cleanly on a DB with existing services, existing services with no stored key behave as first clone, and changing the service git URL host clears or re-keys the pinned key so a stale pin neither blocks nor is silently reused for a different host

GIT_HOST_KEY_MISMATCH error message, activity events, logs and API responses contain neither the offending nor the pinned key blob (fingerprint at most), covered by the security:scan-leaks canary or an equivalent assertion; remote ssh stderr is not echoed raw

noodara services reset-host-key validates the serviceId argument (UUID, else exit non-zero with a named error and no DB write), is idempotent on a service with no pinned key, returns non-zero for an unknown service without revealing other data, and takes effect on the next deploy

tasks.title: Deploy: fail stale QUEUED deployments when enqueue and undo both fail

acceptance.text: The worker's startup sweep and its repeatable reconcile tick move a QUEUED deployment older than a threshold (env, default 2 min) and without a BullMQ job to FAILED/ENQUEUE_FAILED through the domain state machine
A QUEUED deployment whose job exists, or that is younger than the threshold, is never touched; the transition is race-safe against a worker that picks it up at the same time
The integration test reproduces Postgres+Redis down during enqueue, brings them back, and sees the deployment end FAILED/ENQUEUE_FAILED with deployment.updated published and the 409 lock released

The stale-QUEUED threshold env is range-validated (minimum above the longest legitimate enqueue-to-pickup delay, such as the BullMQ backoff, and a maximum) with a named boot error, listed in turbo.json passThroughEnv and .env.example per ADR 0003

The sweep decision uses an authoritative BullMQ job lookup with a Redis error treated as unknown (skip, retry next tick), never as 'no job'; a Redis outage during the sweep must not fail healthy QUEUED deployments, and the sweep is idempotent when run twice or by two workers concurrently (conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status='QUEUED', one activity event)

The ENQUEUE_FAILED failure writes an activity event and deployment.updated with an actionable closed-vocabulary message and no raw Redis/Postgres error text; the sweep is bounded per tick (batch limit) so a large backlog cannot block the worker

tasks.title: execStreaming: release stdin secrets when the stream ends

acceptance.text: Stdin secrets registered by execStreaming are released exactly once after the last output line is redacted, on success, failure, timeout and cancel
A secret echoed in the final flushed chunk is still redacted (release never runs before the flush)
The stale comment in exec-streaming.ts and OPEN_QUESTIONS #7 wording are updated

A stdin secret that was split across the final two chunks, or echoed after the stream ended with a non-zero exit, is redacted before release; release is idempotent (a second call or a throw in the release path does not leak, double-free another stream's secret, or crash the worker), and a concurrent execStreaming call holding the same secret value keeps its own registration

The registered stdin secrets are not retained after release (heap or registry size returns to baseline after N streams, including aborted ones), proven with a loop test that asserts the Redactor registry is empty

tasks.title: Build cache prune policy (D12): age-based, once a day per server

acceptance.text: After a SUCCESS deployment, an allowlisted docker builder prune -f --filter until=168h runs with an explicit timeout, at most once per server per 24 h (Redis key with TTL)
A prune failure or timeout is logged by error class only and never changes the deployment's status
The integration test proves the prune runs once on two consecutive deployments and does not delete the running container's image
ADR 0009 records the policy, the host-wide impact and how to disable it (NOODARA_BUILD_CACHE_PRUNE=off)

The prune filter and age come from validated constants or env (NOODARA_BUILD_CACHE_PRUNE accepts only on|off, other values fail boot with a named error), the template takes no free strings, and a prune never runs while another deployment on the same server is BUILDING (skipped, retried on a later deployment)

The Redis once-per-24h key is set atomically (SET NX with TTL) before the prune so two concurrent deployments on one server run one prune; on Redis failure the prune is skipped, not run unbounded, and a failed prune releases or shortens the key so it is retried rather than silenced for 24 h

The prune never exceeds a hard timeout and its output (which can list cache IDs) is not persisted or published to build logs; with NOODARA_BUILD_CACHE_PRUNE=off no prune command is issued, proven with a fake port

tasks.title: Integration harness: clear precheck when port 3000 is taken

acceptance.text: If port 3000 is in use, pnpm test:integration fails at once with a message that names the port and how to free it, not EADDRINUSE deep in boot-command
With port 3000 free the boot suite is green; OPEN_QUESTIONS #3 is resolved
